name: Abdykhamit Beknur
role: Validated domain models, quotation, confirmation, pricing and reports

blocks.heading: Assigned implementation scope
paragraphs: Project: ASTRA Space Travel Agency; group IT-2512; teammate Zhumazhan Miras. The assigned modules provide validated flight and reservation values, immutable state, pricing, quotation, confirmation and current-state reports. Their source is Astra.Core/Reservations: Flight.cs, Reservation.cs, ReservationState.cs, ReservationPricing.cs, ReservationBooking.cs and AgencyReports.cs.

blocks.heading: Factories and coherent state
paragraphs: Flight.Create validates identity, destination, departure, capacity and exact-cent base fare. Reservation.Create validates passengers, money and status-dependent cancellation data. Private constructors and getter-only properties prevent unchecked construction and property edits. ReservationState.Create snapshots input collections and checks duplicate IDs, flight references, dates and capacity. AvailableSeats derives occupancy from confirmed reservations, avoiding a second mutable counter. FindFlight and FindReservation expose absence through Option rather than ambiguous null values.

blocks.heading: Quotation, confirmation and reporting
paragraphs: ReservationBooking.Quote composes ValidateRequest, CheckAvailability and CalculateQuote through Bind. Missing, closed, departed or full flights stop before pricing. Reserve rejects reused IDs, creates a confirmed reservation and returns a new ReservationChange only after state validation. Miras's transfer workflow reuses Quote; the application layer persists successful changes.

ReservationPricing.CreatePolicy captures PricingConfig once. Standard, Group10 and Family5 vary one business rule without mutable global switches. AgencyReports.Build filters upcoming flights and groups stored contracts by destination. Occupancy sorts by free seats then flight ID; finance sorts by retained value then destination. Both reports materialise immutable arrays, preserving deterministic repeated access.

For four Premium passengers on the 49000 USD Moon fare, Standard produces 264600 USD, Group10 238140 USD and Family5 251370 USD. Quotation leaves the snapshot unchanged; confirmation consumes capacity in a new snapshot. Console output and JSON saving remain application-layer responsibilities.

blocks.heading: Specific assertions
paragraphs: The first six methods below are in Astra.Tests/ReservationBookingTests.cs; the report method is in AgencyWorkflowTests.cs. Expected values come directly from assertions. Measured outcomes are attached from the test-run results.

tests.expected: Changing caller lists leaves one flight, no reservations and 12 free seats in the created snapshot.
Four Moon Premium passengers: Standard 264600, Group10 238140, Family5 251370 USD; quoting creates no booking.
Quantities 0 and 7 or class 99 fail; the supplied pricing delegate is called zero times.
Two last seats cost 98000 USD and leave zero free; the original retains two free seats; another booking fails.
Four slightly negative/over-limit raw amounts fail both Quote and Reserve; original state remains empty with 12 free seats.
Raw amounts 0 and 10800000000 are accepted and retained exactly in the confirmed contract.
Ties order flights A then B and destinations Mars then Moon; a cancelled 100 USD contract with 50 refund retains 50.

blocks.heading: Why these techniques fit
paragraphs: Bind represents a dependent stage that can fail; Map wraps the final successful state as a change result. Private factories establish invariants once, while immutable snapshots let unsuccessful operations leave earlier values untouched. Delegate counters prove short-circuit behaviour, beyond merely checking an error message. Partial application keeps policy configuration separate from requests. The same four-passenger request demonstrates an observable tariff difference, and deterministic tie-breakers make reports stable for equal totals.

blocks.heading: A range check hidden by rounding
paragraphs: Review exposed a concrete defect in ReservationBooking.CalculateQuote: the policy result was rounded before checking the permitted monetary range. A raw -0.001 became 0.00 and escaped the negative-value check. Similarly, 10800000000.001 rounded down to the maximum supported total and was accepted although the raw value exceeded the limit.

The corrected sequence stores rawAmount, rejects values below zero or above ReservationRules.MaximumTotal, and only then rounds to cents using AwayFromZero. Overflow remains an explicit Result failure. RoundingCannotHideAnOutOfRangePolicyResult covers -0.001, -0.004, 10800000000.001 and 10800000000.004 through both quotation and confirmation. ExactPolicyRangeBoundariesRemainValid confirms that valid endpoints still work. Validation therefore checks the business rule rather than its rounded representation.

blocks.heading: Integration and responsibility boundary
paragraphs: The earlier fixed destination schedule could not represent two departures with different fares and capacities. Validated Flight identifiers now separate a destination from an individual flight. State-derived availability supports confirmation, cancellation and transfer without synchronising independent seat counters.

Beknur's assigned scope is the domain foundation and pure reports. Miras's assigned scope consumes these models for changes, CLI parsing, persistence and export. Shared integration tests exercise both areas; they are not attributed exclusively to one student. The preserved Result, Option and earlier assignment modules are shared foundations.

blocks.heading: Limits of this implementation
paragraphs: Quotations and balances are contractual calculations, not bank payments. Reports describe current stored contracts, including refunds; transfers do not retain a historical transaction ledger. Snapshots use O(n) memory. There is no flight-editing interface or passenger identity model. Explicit dates support reproducible tests rather than an authenticated transaction clock.
